framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Central: Mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisition of shares; triggers when a person or group acquires 25% or 10% (or such other threshold) in a listed company. Non-compliance attracts penalties and potential trading restrictions.
Central: Defines 'acquirer', 'concert party', 'control', and 'group' — critical to determining if family entities and trusts are deemed a concert party for aggregate holding disclosure.
Central: Lists exemptions from open offer (intra-promoter transfers, inheritance, etc.); family restructuring may qualify if conditions are met.
Relevant: Statutory definition of control; informs concert party analysis for family-held entities.

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations, 2011 — Regulation 15-17 (open offer requirements)
framework.note: Central: May be triggered unless exemption applies; specifies offer price, quantity, and timeline.
Amended: Stock exchanges enforce disclosure norms; check current circular on timing and form of Reg. 31 filings.

headline: Deepak Shriram Family Entities File SEBI Takeover Disclosure for Shriram Pistons & Rings
sum: Multiple entities linked to the Deepak Shriram family and associated trusts have filed a Regulation 31(4) substantial acquisition of shares disclosure with NSE relating to Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited, signalling a family restructuring or consolidation of holdings.
detail: The disclosure was submitted to NSE by or on behalf of the Deepak Shriram family entities, including the Family Benefit Trust, multiple private companies (Sarva, Sera Com, Manish, Shabnam Commercial), individual family members (Meenakshi Das, Luv Deepak Shriram, Nandishi Shriram, Kush Deepak Shriram), and Nak Benefit Trust. The filing is formal notice under SEBI regulation 31(4) of the Takeover Code (2011), which mandates disclosure of substantial acquisitions of shares. The specific percentage acquired, consideration, and timing of the underlying transaction remain to be corroborated from company disclosures or exchange filings.
